extracted.intended_audience: prospective NEH applicants and grantees (humanities scholars, public programmers, cultural institutions, media producers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of NEH grant programs and what kinds of projects each program supports (e.g., media projects, public humanities programs, preservation grants, book fellowships). Useful for matching a humanities project to an appropriate NEH funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Media Projects program supports the development, production, and distribution of radio programs, podcasts, long-form documentary films, and documentary film series that engage general audiences with humanities ideas in creative and appealing ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended formats include radio, podcasts, long-form documentary films, and documentary film series; emphasis is on engaging general audiences with humanities ideas in a creative and appealing manner. (Page also lists an upcoming deadline: January 12, 2022 — Division of Public Programs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Humanities Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Humanities Projects grants support projects that bring the ideas and insights of the humanities to life for general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on public-facing work that translates humanities ideas for general audiences; applicants should design programs that make humanities content accessible and engaging to non-specialist publics. (Page lists an upcoming deadline: January 12, 2022 — Division of Public Programs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation Assistance Grants for Smaller Institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Helps small and mid-sized institutions—such as libraries, museums, and colleges and universities—improve their ability to preserve and care for their significant humanities collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted to small and mid-sized institutions (examples given: libraries, museums, colleges and universities). Focus is capacity-building for preservation and care of significant humanities collections; applicants should demonstrate institutional need and capacity to use preservation assistance effectively. (Upcoming deadline listed: January 13, 2022 — Division of Preservation and Access.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports well-researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for authors producing well-researched humanities books with the explicit goal of reaching a broad/general readership; proposals should demonstrate both scholarly rigor and public-facing appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project-to-program fit / match your project to a grant program
rubrics_metrics.description: Match Your Project to a Grant Program (page navigation item implying applicants should align their proposal with the most appropriate NEH program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to identify and apply to the specific NEH program whose aims and eligible formats best fit their project. Use program descriptions, examples of previously funded projects, and guidance for first-time applicants to determine fit before submitting.
